Abstract
This paper considers an integrated supplier selection and inventory control problem for
a multi-echelon inventory system with an order-splitting policy. A buyer firm consisting
of one warehouse and
N

potential suppliers; the acquisition of the warehouse takes place when the inventory level

echelon system, and formulate the supplier selection problem in a Mixed Integer Nonlinear

1. Introduction
Supply chain outsourcing has become mainstream, driven by digitalization, globalization,
and ever evolving customer expectations. In today’s increasingly globalized economy, com-
panies face mounting challenges to reducing their operational costs and enlarging their profit
margins with regard to procurement and outsourcing (Tsay et al., 2018; Hosseini et al., 2019;
Kaur and Prakash Singh, 2021; Hashmi et al., 2021). According to a Gartner study, 80% of
the respondents planned to significantly increase their logistics outsourcing budget beyond
warehousing and fulfillment in 2020 (Gatner, 2019). As an enabling competitive advantage,
outsourcing is widely recognized as a proven way to cut down operational cost, embraced by
93% of the organizations that are adopting or considering cloud solutions (Deloitte, 2018).
As modern supply chains have evolved from simple, linear connections between businesses
and suppliers to interconnected and interdependent networks spanning across organizations,
nations, and continents, it is critical for most industries to form an effective sourcing strat-
egy (Hamdan and Cheaitou, 2017; Yousefi et al., 2021; Li et al., 2021a). This has become
a renewed focus as the fallout of COVID-19 (Deloitte, 2020), which put a serve strain on

authors developed a mixed-integer programming (MIP) model for the supplier selection
problem. The MIP model incorporated inventory decisions, inventory capacity constraints,
specific delivery frequency, and transportation capacity based on multiple products and time
periods.

The supplier selection problem has three major decisions: (1) Which supplier should be
selected? (2) How much should be ordered? (3) When should the order occur? With regard
to these questions, the choice of suppliers is closely intertwined with the inventory control
model. Incorporating decisions to trigger orders over time into decisions about supplier
selection and order allocation may significantly reduce costs, especially over a long planning
horizon (Aissaoui et al., 2007; Guo and Li, 2014; Kaur and Prakash Singh, 2021).
One important problem related to this area is the integration of inventory lot-sizing
and supplier selection, that is, situations in which buyers can simultaneously select the
most suitable suppliers for each period and optimize the lot size of each product. For
example, Haq and Kannan (2006) developed an integrated supplier selection and multi-
echelon distribution inventory model. Similar models in supplier selection and inventory
lot-sizing can also be found in (Demirtas and Ustun, 2009; Mendoza and Ventura, 2010;
Hammami et al., 2012). Although all these studies incorporated inventory decisions with
supplier selection, inventory control policies were not considered because the inventory cost

problem and the inventory control problem in a serial supply chain with an order-splitting
policy. The strategy we work with, of pooling lead-time risks by splitting replenishment
orders among multiple suppliers simultaneously, is an attractive sourcing policy that has
captured the attention of both academic researchers and corporate managers (Sazvar et al.,
2014). In this work, we consider a two-echelon distribution system with a central warehouse

5. Conclusions
In this research, a supplier selection and order allocation problem in a multi-echelon
system under stochastic demand was investigated under the broad context of outsourcing.
We simultaneously considered the supplier selection decisions, among potential suppliers, as
well as the inventory control policies, among one warehouse and
N
identical retailers. We
adopted an order-splitting assumption in which a warehouse order was split simultaneously
among all the selected suppliers. In addition to the system costs, such as ordering, holding,
and back-order costs, this study took into account the capacity and reliability rate as the
supplier selection criteria. We developed a mixed integer non-linear programming (MINLP)
model to select the best suppliers and determined both the reorder point and the order-split
quantities simultaneously at each supply chain echelon so that the total expected profit was
maximized. Unlike most similar works in the literature, the proposed model is multi-echelon,
and multi-period. To the best of our knowledge, a supplier selection model that considers
all of these aspects does not exist in the literature. We conducted extensive numerical
experiments that demonstrate the solvability of the problems and effectiveness of the model.
Furthermore, we investigated some issues regarding long-distance supplier selection. Finally,
a sensitivity analysis for the long-distance suppliers was conducted.
